subject: Targeted egress degradation affecting APAC/EU — mitigation steps and postmortem plan

Subject: Initial notification: APAC/EU egress degradation affecting Acme Retail — immediate reroute guidance

Hi Susan / Acme infra team,

Quick heads-up — our monitoring picked up elevated egress errors from the APAC and EU edge clusters routing into Acme Retail's tenancy starting ~09:05 UTC. Impact is best-effort for short-lived requests (higher 5xxs and longer tail latencies).

What we're doing now:
- Flipped emergency routing policy to prefer dedicated EU/SG-hosted pools for your traffic to reduce cross-region egress.
- Throttling burst window lowered to keep tail latency contained.
- Opening support ticket SUP-8721 and starting an incident bridge; I'll share notes and a measurement export shortly.

Immediate ask for you:
1) If you have local egress routing rules that prefer regional endpoints, please confirm whether you want us to pin to EU-only for the next 2 hours.
2) If any critical jobs are time-sensitive, flag them now and we'll prioritize their tokens through a reserved queue.

I'm looping Marcus and Lauren for a technical and account-side run-through. Expect a short action playbook in the next 15 min.

— Olga

Subject: Re: Initial notification: APAC/EU egress degradation affecting Acme Retail — immediate reroute guidance

Hi Susan — confirmed: we've pinned Acme traffic to EU-only pools and elevated priority for the 10:30 UTC bulk job. Expected behavior and mitigation steps below.

Short-term impact (what to expect in next 2 hours):
- Error rate should fall by ~60% once pinned; we estimate remaining increased tail latency of +40–80ms due to queueing in dedicated pools.
- No data loss; requests will be routed through verified EU pools.

Actionable steps for Acme (recommended):
1) If possible, enable client-side exponential backoff with jitter for 500/502 responses for the next 2 hours.
2) Disable synchronous retries for non-idempotent checkout calls until we publish a full post-incident note.
3) Confirm whether you want us to run a short QA sweep inside your staging tenant (we can run smoke queries targeting search + checkout at 09:55 UTC).

Attachments: egress-egress-kpi-extract-20290418.csv (30s aggregated metrics), redwood-reroute-playbook-v1.pdf

I'll keep this thread updated; Marcus will chime in with the technical details and timeline for a full RCA.

Olga

Subject: Technical note: fallback routing, KV cache, and expected perf tradeoffs

Hi Susan / Acme infra team — quick technical status update from the runtime side: 

Root of current symptoms (short): a mis-signal from an upstream peering provider caused intermittent packet drops on the APAC→EU egress path, increasing retransmits and producing bursty 5xxs on edge nodes. The cluster-level health filter then began redistributing sessions to a smaller set of EU pools which produced the observed queueing.

What we applied (already live):
- Emergency route pin to EU-dedicated capacity for Acme tenancy.
- Reduced concurrent connection handoffs to allow KV cache warm-up (improves cache hit rate for retries).
- Applied temporary conservative batching window (reduces token throughput but stabilizes tail latency).

Expected impact and tradeoffs:
- Latency: +40–120ms on heavy payloads (large embedding/long-context calls).
- Cost: Slight increase in per-token compute due to smaller batches; we'll submit cost impact notes separately for your accounting team.
- Duration: If upstream peering remains unstable we'll open a peering escalation with the provider; otherwise we expect traffic to normalize within 4–6 hours.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 20-min technical bridge with your infra ops and our network team at 10:15 UTC.

— Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem & next steps: APAC/EU egress incident (SUP-8721) — root cause and remediation plan

Hi Susan / Acme team,

Thanks for your patience during the incident. Below is a concise postmortem and the actions we will take with timelines. Full technical RCA (network traces, configurations) is attached in the Drive link.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2029-04-18T09:05:00Z — 2029-04-18T13:12:00Z (root cause resolved by upstream peering partner; residual routing normalization through 2029-04-18T14:00:00Z).
- Impact: Elevated 5xx rates and tail latency for requests routed through APAC and EU egress paths. Acme saw increased client errors primarily in checkout/search for ~4 hours.
- Root cause: A degraded intermediate provider peering session caused packet loss on APAC→EU backbone, triggering cluster redistribution and queueing on smaller EU pools.

Immediate remediations completed:
- Emergency pinning: We added per-tenant emergency pin rules to prefer nearby dedicated pools when upstream peering anomalies are detected (completed 2029-04-18T09:20:00Z).
- Retry guidance: We published temporary client-side retry guidance and coordinated a staged QA sweep with Acme.
- Monitoring: New alert rule added to detect anomalous retransmit rates at the egress layer.

Planned long-term fixes (timeline):
- 30 days: Automated peering health scoring and per-tenant fallback thresholds (owner: Netops).
- 60 days: Expand EU and APAC spare capacity pools to reduce redistribution impact (owner: Capacity Planning).
- 90 days: Post-deployment testing harness for simulated peering loss to validate reroute automations (owner: Runtime QA).

Customer follow-ups:
- We'll share a CSV with token-level latency deltas and a short cost projection for the pinning period by EOD tomorrow.
- Offer: 1 month of usage credit applied to Acme's April invoice as a goodwill gesture; billing team will follow up if you accept.

If you want a synchronous walk-through of the RCA, we can set a 30-min session this week with Marcus and Rishi.

Appreciate the close collaboration.

— Olga
